prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
U0001: Revision: Rev A Document No: CTSD-ADV-1788 Effective Date: November, 2023 Page: Page 12 of 110 Title: Concept of Operations 1 Introduction The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is embarking on a 21st century space exploration initiative via the Moon to Mars and Artemis programs.1 These programs aim to es- tablish a sustained lunar presence and explore the moon’s surface using innovative technologies.
U0002: One primary goal of these initiatives is to enable crew autonomy.
U0003: The existing human spaceflight work domain must undergo a substantial transformation to redistribute and create work capabilities among future flight teams, which includes both crew and Earth based mission support personnel.
U0004: For example, crew will be given greater access to a variety of information to make locally informed decisions.
U0005: The broader flight team will need to simultaneously interact with this data and provide new means of support throughout the mission as crew take on more responsibility and authority.
U0006: Achieving increased crew autonomy will require new technologies and operational concepts to fa- cilitate information exchange among the flight team and crew in future planetary exploration work demands.
U0007: To meet these demands, NASA proposed requirements for a digital display for an EVA spacesuit to provide relevant information to the crew member.
U0008: The Joint Augmented Reality Visual Informatics System (Joint AR) project pursued four years of research and development towards a suit-display system in a near-eye, AR form factor.
U0009: The project was responsible for developing software (cus- tom graphics engine and core flight software), physical hardware prototyping (controls, projection display optics, suited display platform), virtual prototyping platform (a virtual reality testbed), and human-in-the-loop (HITL) operational testing informed by EVA flight controllers, crew members, and human factors engineers for con-ops definition.
U0010: This document contains substantial updates to CTSD-ADV-1788 Rev.
U0011: Basic.
U0012: This revision was pro- duced by the project to summarize the use-cases and and user experiences developed throughout the project, and refine the Basic revision originally drafted at the beginning of the project life cycle. 1.1 Purpose The primary purpose of this document is to summarize and make available the scenario devel- opment efforts that have been pursued and explored within the Joint AR project.
U0013: This includes descriptions of the scenarios themselves as well as corresponding potential of advanced informat- ics displays to support those specified scenarios.
U0014: In doing so, this document provides a variety of approaches to deconstruct and hypothesize how future technological capabilities so that with future EVA work demands can be satisfied within future human planetary spaceflight missions. 1.2 Scope The scope of this document is intended to support two audiences: 1) on-going NASA and vendor efforts to enable advanced informatics for EVA operations and 2) researchers and technology de- velopers in the broader academic and commercial sector.
U0015: This document extends the spacesuit informatics concepts found within published NASA documentation by exploring a variety of possi- ble envisioned futures to help imagine and describe what future EVA operations could look like with crew having decision support capabilities via an advanced informatics display.
U0016: The contents of this document are applicable to any advanced informatics development efforts. 1For more information: https://www.nasa.gov/MoonToMarsArchitecture Revision: Rev A Document No: CTSD-ADV-1788 Effective Date: November, 2023 Page: Page 13 of 110 Title: Concept of Operations This document is neither prescriptive, nor definitive in offering solutions.
U0017: Instead, this document of- fers a deliberate attempt to articulate the simultaneous creation of both the situated work demands of future EVA operations and the corresponding value propositions of Joint AR capabilities.
U0018: In do- ing so, a shared vision of future EVA operations can be distilled to inform subsequent work domain development efforts in conjunction with technological development. 1.3 Change Authority and Responsibility Proposed changes to this document shall be submitted to JSC-EV3 for consideration and disposi- tion. 2 On the Path to Enabling Earth-Independence In 2023, NASA released its Moon-to-Mars Architecture Definition Document.
U0019: This architecture document serves to set the baseline goals to create a systems engineering framework for the necessary program contributions to return to the Moon and journey on to Mars.
U0020: Furthermore, this architecture has established high level objectives in a variety of domains including science, infrastructure, transportation and habitation, and operations.
U0021: Meeting these objectives will provide the scientific and technical capabilities for sustained lunar and eventual Martian presence. “The implementation of Earth-independent missions will be one of the biggest challenges facing a sustained space presence.
